project.name: SpendCube Phase 6 - Recommendations and Review Workstation

summary: Phase 6 of 6 — final phase. Builds the recommendation engine (rule-based with LLM narrative generation) and the review workstation UI (supplier match review, category review, manual overrides, audit trail). Wires recommendations into the dashboard as page 06. Wires review workstation as page 07. Validation gate: at least 5 recommendation types generate from test data, review workflows function end-to-end, manual corrections persist and feed back into future pipeline runs.

decisions.recommendations_approach: Rule-based first — generate all recommendations deterministically from cube metrics. LLM used only to generate consulting-quality narrative text (optional, dry_run skips). Recommendations stored as DataFrame and exported to data/output/recommendations.json.
decisions.recommendation_schema: Each recommendation: type, category/supplier (context), evidence (string), estimated_impact_aud (float), confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), action (string), lever (string), assumptions (list). Sorted by estimated_impact_aud desc.
decisions.review_workstation: Streamlit page 07. Shows supplier match review queue (from supplier_match_log where review_status=PENDING) and category review queue (from transactions where category_confidence < 0.60). Approve/reject/override buttons write to DB and audit_log.
decisions.audit_trail: Every manual action in review workstation writes to audit_log_table (defined in src/models/database.py Phase 1): table_name, record_id, field_name, old_value, new_value, changed_by, changed_at.
decisions.feedback_loop: Approved supplier matches update supplier_master. Approved category overrides insert into category_overrides_table. Both feed into next pipeline run automatically.
decisions.savings_levers: 14 lever types from spec. Rules engine generates whichever are applicable. Minimum 5 guaranteed: SUPPLIER_CONSOLIDATION, PAYMENT_TERM_EXTENSION, TAIL_SPEND_RATIONALISATION, CONTRACT_COMPLIANCE, MAVERICK_SPEND.
decisions.phase_foundation: All phases 1-5 complete. Cube built, all 5 dashboard pages working. recommendations/rules.py, narratives.py, engine.py are placeholders. dashboard/pages/06_recommendations.py and 07_review_workstation.py are placeholders.

existing_tables.transactions: Full canonical schema with category/supplier fields — source for recommendations
existing_tables.category_overrides: Manual category corrections — written by review workstation
existing_tables.audit_log: Every manual action logged here — table_name, record_id, field_name, old/new value, changed_by, changed_at

patterns_to_follow: Same module CLI pattern as all prior phases
LLM calls gated on config.llm.dry_run — skip narrative generation when dry_run=true
Review workstation writes to DB then clears st.cache_data to force refresh
Audit log entry on every write: use insert_audit_log(engine, table, record_id, field, old, new, changed_by='system') helper

userStories.title: Implement rule-based recommendation engine
userStories.description: Implement src/recommendations/rules.py with all rule-based recommendation generators. These run deterministically from cube metrics — no LLM. Must generate at least 5 recommendation types from the 10-row sample data.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/recommendations/rules.py — implement RecommendationRules class
__init__(self, cube: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], metrics: dict, config): stores cube and metrics
Implement generate_all(self) -> list[dict]: calls all rule methods, returns sorted list of recommendation dicts

Implement rule_supplier_consolidation(self) -> list[dict]: for each L2 category with > config.recommendations.consolidation_threshold (5) suppliers, generate SUPPLIER_CONSOLIDATION rec. estimated_impact = category_spend * config.recommendations.consolidation_saving_pct (0.08). Evidence: '{n} suppliers in {category}, top supplier = {pct}%'.

Implement rule_payment_term_extension(self) -> list[dict]: for each supplier in top 50 by spend where weighted_avg_terms < config.recommendations.target_payment_days (45), generate PAYMENT_TERM_EXTENSION. estimated_impact = (target - current) / 365 * annual_spend * config.recommendations.wacc. Filter: only if estimated_impact > config.recommendations.min_wc_opportunity (10000). Evidence: 'Current: {n} days, Target: {t} days'.

Implement rule_tail_spend_rationalisation(self) -> list[dict]: if tail_spend_pct > config.recommendations.tail_spend_alert_pct (0.05), generate TAIL_SPEND_RATIONALISATION. estimated_impact = tail_spend_amount * 0.10. Evidence: '{n} tail suppliers, {pct} of spend'.
Implement rule_maverick_spend(self) -> list[dict]: if maverick_spend_pct > config.recommendations.maverick_alert_pct (0.15), generate CONTRACT_COMPLIANCE. estimated_impact = maverick_spend * 0.05.

Implement rule_competitive_tender(self) -> list[dict]: for each L2 category with single supplier (count=1) and spend > 50000 AUD, generate COMPETITIVE_TENDER rec. estimated_impact = category_spend * 0.07.
Implement rule_contract_coverage_gap(self) -> list[dict]: for each L1 category where contract_coverage_pct < 0.50 and spend > 20000, generate CONTRACT_COVERAGE_GAP rec.
Each recommendation dict: {type, context (category or supplier name), evidence, estimated_impact_aud (float), confidence ('HIGH'/'MEDIUM'/'LOW'), action (string), lever (string)}
CLI: python src/recommendations/rules.py --db data/db/spend_cube.db — prints all recommendations sorted by impact

userStories.title: Implement LLM narrative generation
userStories.description: Implement src/recommendations/narratives.py to optionally enrich rule-based recommendations with consulting-quality narrative text using the Claude API. Must skip when dry_run=true.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/recommendations/narratives.py — implement NarrativeGenerator class
__init__(self, config): loads config, initialises anthropic.Anthropic() only if not dry_run

Implement enrich(self, recommendations: list[dict]) -> list[dict]: if dry_run, return recommendations unchanged (narrative field = None). When not dry_run: batch all recommendations into one call. Prompt: 'You are a procurement consultant. For each recommendation, write a concise 2-3 sentence consulting-quality narrative explaining the issue, evidence, and recommended action. Format: JSON array with fields: type, context, narrative.

Recommendations:
{recs_json}'. Parse response, merge narrative back into each rec dict.
Log LLM call via log_llm_call()
Handle API errors: log warning, return recommendations without narrative
CLI: python src/recommendations/narratives.py — with dry_run=true, prints sample recommendations without narrative enrichment

userStories.title: Implement recommendation engine orchestrator and export
userStories.description: Implement src/recommendations/engine.py as the orchestrator that runs rules → narratives → exports to data/output/recommendations.json. Also update Makefile.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/recommendations/engine.py — implement RecommendationEngine class
__init__(self, config, engine): initialises SpendCubeBuilder, CubeMetrics, RecommendationRules, NarrativeGenerator
Implement run(self) -> list[dict]: builds cube → computes metrics → runs rules → enriches with narratives → returns sorted recommendations list
Implement export(self, recommendations: list[dict], path: str = 'data/output/recommendations.json') -> str: saves to JSON, returns path
Implement to_dataframe(self, recommendations: list[dict]) -> pd.DataFrame: returns DataFrame with columns: type, context, evidence, estimated_impact_aud, confidence, action, lever, narrative

Edit file: Makefile — no separate target needed; recommendations are generated as part of build-cube pipeline. Update build-cube target to also run: python src/recommendations/engine.py --db data/db/spend_cube.db
CLI: python src/recommendations/engine.py --db data/db/spend_cube.db — runs full engine, prints recommendations table sorted by impact

Verify: python src/recommendations/engine.py --db data/db/spend_cube.db — generates at least 3 recommendations from the 10-row sample data (maverick, tail spend, contract coverage gap are most likely)

userStories.title: Implement review workstation — supplier match queue
userStories.description: Implement the supplier match review queue section of dashboard/pages/07_review_workstation.py. Shows PENDING supplier matches for human approval/rejection, with approve/reject/merge actions that persist to DB.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: dashboard/pages/07_review_workstation.py — implement review workstation page (supplier section)
Page title: 'Review Workstation'
Section: 'Supplier Match Review' with st.subheader
Load supplier_match_log rows where review_status='PENDING' from SQLite. Sort by confidence asc (lowest confidence first), then by spend desc.

For each pending match, show: st.expander(f'{raw_supplier_name} → {canonical_supplier_name} (conf: {confidence:.2f})'). Inside: show raw_supplier_id, match_method, evidence string, proposed canonical_supplier_name. Three buttons: ✅ Approve, ❌ Reject, ✏️ Override (text input for manual canonical name).

On Approve: UPDATE supplier_match_log SET review_status='APPROVED', reviewed_at=now WHERE id=?. INSERT audit_log entry. UPDATE transactions SET canonical_supplier_id/name = approved values WHERE raw_supplier_name=?. Clear st.cache_data.
On Reject: UPDATE supplier_match_log SET review_status='REJECTED'. INSERT audit_log. Clear cache.
On Override: create new supplier_master entry if needed, set review_status='APPROVED', update transactions. INSERT audit_log.
Show count: 'X matches pending review' header metric.

queries.check_audit_log: python -c "import pandas as pd; from sqlalchemy import create_engine; e=create_engine('sqlite:///data/db/spend_cube.db'); df=pd.read_sql('SELECT * FROM audit_log LIMIT 5', e); print(df)"

checks: ≥5 recommendation types generated from 1000-row test data
Approving supplier match updates transactions table
Audit trail logged for all review workstation actions
Full pipeline runs end-to-end on 1000-row test data without errors

risks: Review workstation DB writes in Streamlit: st.cache_data must be cleared after every write or UI will show stale data. Use st.cache_data.clear() after each DB mutation.

Small sample data for recommendations: 10-row sample may not trigger all recommendation rules (e.g. supplier consolidation needs >5 suppliers in same category). Use 1000-row test data for integration validation.
Concurrent DB writes: SQLite doesn't support concurrent writes well. Review workstation is single-user so this is acceptable for v1.
Recommendations JSON schema: must be stable — dashboard page and export depend on it. Define the schema explicitly in engine.py docstring.
outOfScope: Supplier risk scoring beyond data quality flags
